correctness.rationale: Monomial rigidity is a valid antecedent theorem for perfect evolution algebras and the weighted cycle structure matrix is invertible. Rotation and diagonal scaling exhaust all isomorphisms. A telescoping N-th-power invariant with a constructive recursion proves the iff class criterion; exact kernel and orbit stabilizers and Möbius inversion yield class counts and automorphism orders. The two F_4 cases are distinguished by invariant classes; direct explicit generators prove C_3 semidirect C_n and C_(3n/2), and elementary cyclic subgroup theory proves nonsplitting exactly when 3 divides n/2. Finite exhaustive orbit enumeration and explicit automorphism equations separately passed; universal claims rest on proof.

value.rationale: All weighted directed-cycle algebras in scope are simple perfect objects, so their field-sensitive isomorphism census and full automorphism order spectrum are structural invariants rather than arbitrary numerical slices. Over F_4 the theorem determines both abstract group types, and the infinite nonsplit C_(9k) family in dimensions 6k gives a concrete natural extension phenomenon not previously covered by the inspected 6-dimensional different-graph example. It explicitly answers the split-versus-nonsplit automorphism-extension question on the whole F_4 weighted single-cycle family, a motivated slice of Question 33 in arxiv:2610.22248.
